meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-22; Start: 15:30 UTC; Duration: ~55 minutes; Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Singh (Nova Health CTO), Sam Carter (Head of ML Ops), Alex Kim (Infra Engineer)
summary: POC scoping for Nova Health to evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Discussed success criteria (latency p95, throughput, cost), workload sizing (sequence lengths, concurrency), required benchmarks and timelines (2-4 week poc, 2-week benchmark runs), security requirements (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, VPC), and next steps for pricing, dataset access, and security deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — happy holidays and we'll try to keep this tight. quick intros?
[00:22] Dr. Priya Singh: Priya here, CTO at Nova Health, we own the roadmap for the clinical AI interfaces.
[00:30] Sam Carter: Sam, head of MLOps, I run infra and manage pipelines.
[00:38] Alex Kim: Alex, infra eng, I handle networking and VPCs.
[00:42] Marco Ruiz: Marco from Redwood (SE) — I'll own the bench and sizing.
[00:46] Lena Park: Cool, agenda is POC scoping: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and then deployment mode recommendation — hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[01:10] Dr. Priya Singh: High level — we need to replace a legacy NLU layer for triage and summarization. Key success is latency p95 under 400ms for single-turn requests and output quality comparable to latest open models. Also data handling — PHI shouldn't leave region unless encrypted and contractually allowed.
[01:40] Sam Carter: To add, cost is a big consideration. We expect ~150 qps peak for embedding/query path and about 30 qps for gen endpoints. Concurrency per model around 80 sessions.
[02:05] Marco Ruiz: Helpful. can you confirm average token lengths? and what models are you currently testing?
[02:12] Sam Carter: Typical prompts average 180 tokens, responses ~120 tokens. We're prototyping on a fine-tuned Llama-2-ish open variant and comparing to a hosted blackbox.
[02:33] Lena Park: Great, that helps. Quick callout on modes: Hosted is fastest to run and simplest (no infra), Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, Private (VPC/on-prem) is for regulatory + data residency. we'll map your criteria to those tradeoffs.
[03:05] Alex Kim: For Nova Health, the main gating is PHI residency and KMS key control. We prefer customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; on-prem is on the table if we need full isolation.
[03:26] Marco Ruiz: Understood. Technically, Dedicated can offer VPC peering + bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations; we also support private control plane for enterprise. Private on-prem gives you full network isolation but is heavier to integrate and takes longer.
[03:50] Dr. Priya Singh: Timeline wise, we want a decision within 6 weeks to start pilot by February. So POC needs to be short and conclusive.
[04:02] Lena Park: That's doable. Typical Redwood POC: week 0 prep / dataset handoff, 1-2 weeks for benchmark runs, 1 week for evaluation and audit + decision. We usually recommend a 3-4 week window for meaningful results.
[04:20] Sam Carter: For benchmarks, what's required from our side? we can provide a representative request set and a redaction script to remove PHI.
[04:36] Marco Ruiz: We'll need: (1) sample traffic traces and concurrency curve, (2) example prompts/responses, (3) a scoring rubric — latency, p95, avg cost per call, and quality metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/clinician-rated). We'll run both throughput and latency-oriented tests.
[04:58] Alex Kim: Network-wise, expect some back-and-forth — if we do dedicated with VPC peering, we need details on IPs, egress rules, and if private, a box spec.
[05:12] Lena Park: Noted. quick tradeoff: Hosted — fastest, lower ops, but less control over KMS; Dedicated — predictable latency and reserved GPU pools, better for throughput; Private — maximum control and residency but higher ops and longer lead time.
[05:40] Dr. Priya Singh: Can Dedicated satisfy our PHI needs if we use customer-managed KMS and VPC peering?
[05:50] Marco Ruiz: Yes for many customers. We do KMS integrations where you bring the key and we encrypt at rest, plus VPC peering for network isolation. However, private control plane or on-prem is required for strict legal/regulatory constraints where data leaving the customer environment is prohibited.
[06:15] Sam Carter: Performance question — with our expected 150 qps peak, what cluster size do you estimate for Dedicated and what latency can we expect?
[06:28] Marco Ruiz: Ballpark: for a Llama-2-like 13B model quantized to 4-bit with Redwood batching, you'd need roughly 6-8 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady 150 qps at modest latency (p95 around 200-400ms) depending on batching and sequence lengths. For lower-latency 100-200ms you'd want more GPUs or smaller model variants.
[06:55] Lena Park: Also can use caching for prefixes and KV cache for multi-turn clinical dialogs which cuts per-request cost and latency. If you have repeated prompts (templates), we can capture prefixes.
[07:12] Dr. Priya Singh: Our dialogs are semi-structured, so caching could help. Quality-wise, what about quantization artifacts?
[07:20] Marco Ruiz: There's a tradeoff. 4-bit quant is sensible for cost; we recommend validation tests for hallucination/regression. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles based on evals.
[07:35] Sam Carter: On the security side, we need SOC2 cert, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and support for customer KMS/HSM. Also retention policies and capability to delete data on request.
[07:51] Lena Park: We provide SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and support KMS integrations. We'll share our security pack.
[08:00] Alex Kim: For private deployment, what's typical lead time and hardware footprint?
[08:08] Marco Ruiz: Private (cloud private control plane) is usually 4-6 weeks to stand up with networking + security reviews; on-prem could be longer — 8-12 weeks including procurement. Hardware depends on the model fleet; for your use case we'd spec a mix: 4-8x 80GB GPUs for gen models plus capacity for embeddings.
[08:35] Dr. Priya Singh: Cost sensitivity — we need estimates for unit costs (per-call) and a committed capacity quote for Dedicated.
[08:44] Lena Park: We'll provide a committed capacity worksheet with estimated per-token costs and expected monthly bill for different traffic envelopes. We'll include both hosted and dedicated pricing to compare.
[09:02] Sam Carter: For the POC, can we run a short benchmark on hosted first to validate quality then move to Dedicated for throughput testing?
[09:10] Marco Ruiz: Yes. That's a common approach — hosted for rapid quality/functional tests, then Dedicated for perf and cost validation. We can run the same harness against both.
[09:24] Alex Kim: Any concerns about rate-limiting or throttling on hosted during tests?
[09:29] Lena Park: For POC we can increase rate limits; sandbox accounts have quotas but we can enable a bench mode.
[09:36] Dr. Priya Singh: Success criteria we care about: p95 latency < 400ms for gen, embedding latency < 50ms, per-call cost under $0.02 for gen (ballpark), quality score within 5% of our current best model, and full KMS control.
[09:56] Marco Ruiz: We'll translate those into bench targets. Embedding <50ms is achievable with dedicated or optimized hosted endpoints with lighter models. We'll include model-variant comparisons.
[10:10] Sam Carter: How about dataset size? We'll provide ~10k representative queries and 500 human-rated items for quality scoring. is that enough?
[10:18] Marco Ruiz: That's ideal. For statistical confidence, 500 human-rated responses is a good baseline. We'll also run automated metrics.
[10:28] Lena Park: We'll outline the bench plan: 1) functional QA on hosted with sample dataset (3 days), 2) full throughput + latency run on Dedicated (3-7 days), 3) report with cost/latency/quality and recommendation (1 week). Total 3-4 weeks.
[10:52] Dr. Priya Singh: If Dedicated looks promising, what's the procurement cadence?
[10:58] Lena Park: Usually after POC Redwood provides committed capacity pricing; procurement can be done in parallel with legal reviews. For private/on-prem we advise starting procurement early due to hardware lead times.
[11:12] Alex Kim: Our legal needs a data processing agreement, plus confirmation about logs and retention.
[11:18] Lena Park: We'll attach DPA and security pack. I'll flag legal to send those docs.
[11:25] Sam Carter: One more perf nuance: we have multi-turn sessions that keep KV cache — how do you handle session affinity and warm KV caches across pods?
[11:34] Marco Ruiz: Redwood handles KV cache routing and can pin sessions to specific pods to keep KV warm; we also support warm-starting the cache from snapshots for predictable latency. It's an ops knob in Dedicated.
[11:50] Dr. Priya Singh: Good. Also want to confirm that when using customer KMS, Redwood can't decrypt customer blobs — is that correct?
[11:57] Marco Ruiz: Correct — with BYOK KMS integration keys never leave your control. We manage encrypted blobs but can't access plaintext without key release. We'll show architecture diagrams in security pack.
[12:10] Lena Park: Ok let's recap next steps and owners. We'll share pricing + dedicated sizing worksheet (Lena), Marco will send bench plan and test harness and run initial hosted runs, Nova Health to provide dataset access and concurrency curves (Sam/Alex), schedule benchmark week of Jan 4. Also schedule security deep dive week of Jan 11.
[12:38] Dr. Priya Singh: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood's side?
[12:43] Marco Ruiz: None immediate — just need dataset access and network contacts for VPC peering if you want Dedicated.
[12:51] Sam Carter: we'll aim to have dataset and contact info by Dec 27, unless holidays slow us down.
[12:58] Lena Park: Noted. I'll put tentative invites and follow up with docs. Appreciate the time.
[13:06] Alex Kim: Thanks — quick question, do you support hardware-level HSM for keys?
[13:11] Marco Ruiz: We integrate with cloud KMS and some HSM-backed keys depending on region and deployment, will confirm in security pack.
[13:22] Dr. Priya Singh: Ok that's all for now. We'll reconvene after docs and bench plan. Happy holidays.
[13:29] Lena Park: Thanks everyone, bye.
[54:12] (call ended)
